name: Revone
soft_passes: #2 optically centred but the bar cluster nearly touches the bottom safe-zone margin (bottom-heavy)
#4 white bars survive 16px, but the lavender arrow (~1.8:1 on indigo) smears into the field
#7 white bars anchor figure-ground at >4:1; the lavender arrow is the weak link at ~1.8:1
#11 distinctive-ish 3D ribbon arrow, but the whole idiom is template-default 3D stock aesthetic
failures: #1 squircle mask baked into the PNG — corners transparent (alpha 0), art radius ~100px/1024 undercuts Apple's continuous squircle, so the system mask double-rounds
#10 single baked raster, not layered Icon Composer art; background and arrow share the indigo hue, so a tinted/clear/mono render collapses the arrow and the bars lose their ground

palette.background: ramp #6166FC->#4044D5 (diagonal indigo, lighter top-left to darker bottom-right, core ~#575BEE)

light_model: soft studio-3D: key light upper-left, short soft baked contact shadows under each form, glossy specular highlights on bar tops and the arrow ridge; omnidirectional Blender-style fill baked into the raster
devices: inflated/clay 3D bars with rounded extruded tops
lavender 3D ribbon growth-arrow rising to upper-right
monochromatic indigo field with near-white subject (tonal restraint)
rhymes_hint: web 3D-render / claymorphism stock-icon family (Iconscout/Icons8-style 3D fintech & analytics icons) — puffy objects on a vivid single-hue gradient; NOT native Big Sur unified or Liquid Glass
notes: icon.png is a full 1024x1024 render, not a resized web thumbnail — resolution is honest. Mask caveat: art is a pre-rounded squircle (transparent corners) instead of a full-bleed square, the #1 failure. Strong brand coherence: the dark marketing cover (#171717 ground) uses the identical indigo #6166FB as its accent, so the icon is that accent saturated into a full field. The growth metaphor is stated twice (ascending bars + rising arrow) — redundant but instantly nameable. Era is 'custom' because the 3D-render/claymorphism idiom quotes none of Apple's native eras; first non-native icon in the corpus, useful as a negative exemplar of 'reads as web stock, not Mac-native.'
